text.content:
Unless a Storyteller specifically implements these optional systems, all Assamites suffer only the "normal" clan weakness presented in the core rulebook regardless of caste. A Storyteller may levy these weaknesses in addition to the common clan weakness if it suits the chronicle.

Variant Warrior Weakness: Warriors may become addicted to the blood of other Cainites. Each time a warrior tastes Kindred vitae, he must succeed on a Self-Control roll (difficulty equal to the number of blood points ingested + 3) or become addicted; from then on, contact with Cainite vitae requires a Self-Control roll (difficulty 8) or an immediate hunger frenzy. Warriors also suffer stained auras: any degree of success on an Aura Perception inspection automatically reveals signs of diablerie, even if the warrior has never tasted Cainite vitae — widely believed to be a remnant of the judges' practice of ritual diablerie in the Second City.

Variant Sorcerer Weakness: A sorcerer's aura always shows the distinctive signs of blood magic to any observer able to read auras, whether or not the sorcerer actively practices Assamite Sorcery. Any use of a supernatural power for the purpose of perceiving a sorcerer gains a -2 difficulty. Attempts to pierce a sorcerer's supernatural concealment (such as Obfuscate) with an opposed power are treated as one level higher than the observer actually possesses (e.g., Auspex 2 attempting to penetrate a sorcerer's Obfuscate is treated as Auspex 3). These weaknesses give no benefit against observers with no supernatural perception, and do not affect mundane concealment like camouflage.

Variant Vizier Weakness: Every vizier has an Obsessive/Compulsive derangement tied to his highest-rated intellectual or creative Ability (or, lacking such a focus, to the minute details of routine tasks). If the character's focus of effort shifts through experience expenditure, the derangement's focus shifts too (roleplayed gradually, not switched instantly). When active, the vizier's aura flickers with strange whorls that a successful Aura Perception user may probe with an Intelligence + Empathy roll (difficulty of the vizier's Humanity or Path rating): two successes reveal the obsession's focus, four reveal the vizier's Nature.

The Mind's Eye Theatre conversions for the three castes, for chronicles that wish to distinguish them mechanically at character creation:

Warriors: Follow the "default" Assamite profile. The only addition: any use of Aura Perception on a warrior always reveals diablerie in his aura, even on a failed challenge.

Sorcerers (called "viziers" by outsiders in Laws of the Night terminology — no roleplaying adjustment is needed, only the mechanics below):

  • Advantage: All sorcerer characters begin with two Ability Traits spread between Academics, Linguistics, Medicine, Occult, and Science.
  • Disadvantage: Any use of Aura Perception on a sorcerer reveals that he practices blood magic, even without knowledge of Thaumaturgy or Assamite Sorcery, and even if the observer fails the Static Mental Challenge to read his emotional state. All uses of Auspex or other supernatural perception on a sorcerer gain two bonus Traits. An observer using supernatural perception to pierce a sorcerer's Obfuscate is treated as having one more level of the relevant power than she actually possesses for purposes of comparing power levels (e.g., Aura Perception is treated as The Spirit's Touch when penetrating a sorcerer's Obfuscate).

Viziers:

  • Advantage: A vizier begins with two additional levels to apply to any Backgrounds except Generation or Mentor.
  • Disadvantage: A vizier has an Obsessive/Compulsive derangement tied to the creative or intellectual Ability in which he has the most Ability Traits. When active, an observer using Aura Perception on the vizier may make a Static Mental Challenge (difficulty of the vizier's permanent Mental Traits, requiring at least one Ability Trait in Empathy) to learn the derangement's focus.

Assamite Sorcery is mechanically similar to Tremere Thaumaturgy (both channel vampiric vitae through will to alter reality), but the two traditions are not cross-compatible, since a Tremere performs ritual the same way every time while an Assamite sorcerer rarely enacts the same ritual identically twice. A character's Assamite blood magic should be recorded on the character sheet as "Assamite Sorcery," distinct from any other blood magic Discipline (such as Thaumaturgy, Necromancy, or Setite Sorcery) the character might separately learn, with paths and rituals for each tracked independently.

All experience costs to learn "foreign" blood magic paths and rituals (i.e., any blood magic tradition other than Assamite Sorcery) are increased by half (round up) for Assamite sorcerers. Even once learned, invoking a foreign path requires one extra Blood Trait, and foreign rituals take triple the normal casting time and require two extra Mental Traits risked for the desired result.

Assamite sorcerers have access to equivalent teachings for many common blood magic paths and rituals under different names, including (partial list) the Path of Blood, the Path of Conjuring, Movement of the Mind (sometimes a sorcerer's primary path), Hands of Destruction, the Lure of Flames, and rituals such as Defense of the Sacred Haven ("Curtain Will"), Wake with Evening's Freshness ("Black Sunrise"), Communicate with Kindred Sire ("Speak with Sire"), Deflection of Wooden Doom ("Turn the Impaling Shaft"), Bone of Lies ("Stain of Guilt"), and A Touch of Nightshade ("Haqim's Disfavor"), among many others recorded across the sorcerer caste's Great Library.
